### Wake: mandatory order

Ordinary Wake card powers happen once each during Wake and must resolve as much as possible; parts saying “may” remain optional. Rest card powers, by contrast, are optional once each at the end of Rest.

1. **People's Favor**, if held: either put 1 favor from your board on it or return 1 from it to the least-full suit bank (choose among tied banks). Never remove its last favor: at 1, you must add if able; if you have none, nothing happens. If banner is already Mob-side, repeat this choice once. Afterwards, if it has 6+ favor, flip to Mob. A banner becoming Mob at this last step does not retroactively repeat the payment that Wake.
2. If Exile, check Usurper and Visionary wins.
3. If Exile holding Oathkeeper title, flip it to Usurper. Victory was checked **before** this flip.
4. At Salt Flats, Mine or Drowned City, optionally take 1 favor **or** 1 secret from that site: one token total, only if your pawn is there. Remote rule gives no income; an empty site gives nothing, with no bank substitute.

### Act

Take any number of major actions, minor actions and Action powers, in any order, including repeating or taking none, provided you pay each cost. Finish an action before starting another. Spend Supply by moving marker right one space per point. Minor actions use no Supply but may have resource costs. You may end Act with Supply unspent: after refreshing in Rest, add that unspent Supply, capped at the leftmost track space.

### Rest: mandatory order

1. Return favor on denizens/edifices to suit-matching banks.
2. Return secrets on denizens/edifices/relics to your board. Flip facedown secrets on your board faceup.
3. Exile/Chancellor refresh Supply to the space showing their warbands remaining in personal bank. For Chancellor: 18+ gives 6 Supply, 11–17 gives 5, 4–10 gives 4, 0–3 gives 3. For Exile: 9+ gives 6, 4–8 gives 5, 0–3 gives 4. Citizen refreshes to the **exact Chancellor marker space**, including leftmost, not by counting purple warbands.
4. Save remaining unspent Supply: move marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply).
5. At the end of Rest, optionally use Rest powers, each once in chosen order.

## Actions

### Search — 2–4 Supply

Choose either world deck or your pawn's region discard pile, never both. Discard-pile Search costs 2. World-deck Search costs 2 at zero Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, and 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2. Other applicable modifiers still apply.

Draw 3 cards, taking fewer only if the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops you, or a modifier reduces the draw. You cannot voluntarily stop early. From world deck, **draw** one at a time, with no required public showing of drawn card fronts. If a Vision is drawn, **announce that a Vision was drawn** (not necessarily which Vision), stop immediately and increase Visions Drawn by 1. Drawing Visions from a discard does not stop drawing or advance the track. If source empties, draw only what remains; no reshuffle is implied.

Discard all but 1 drawn card **before** playing the remaining card, or discard that last card too. Options:

- **Site:** play faceup at your pawn's site, only below its denizen/edifice capacity. Gain 1 favor from that card's suit bank. With People's Favor you may first discard a card from any site in your region, then play to any site in your region, subject to locks and capacity; discarded and receiving sites can differ.
- **Adviser:** play faceup or facedown. Up to 3 total, including facedown; before exceeding limit discard an adviser, subject to locked cards. If the incoming card changes the adviser limit, check against the new limit before playing it; use the lowest of multiple limits. **Later options:** as a minor action you may play a facedown adviser faceup to a legal destination or discard that facedown adviser; you cannot discard a faceup adviser at will. Place 1 favor on an **empty denizen or intact edifice at your pawn's site** (no favor or secrets already). Gain 2 warbands from personal bank onto board; Citizens gain purple. Relics/ruins are ineligible. Rule is not required, and ruling a remote site does not allow remote Muster.

### Trade — 1 Supply

Choose an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site; no relics/ruins. Choose:

- Put 1 secret on card: gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser, from that card's suit bank.
- Put 2 favor on card: gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. With no matching advisers gain **zero** secrets.

Facedown advisers never match. Finite source exhaustion gives only available favor/warbands; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if a gain is reduced to zero.

### Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost

Recover 1 **facedown relic at your site** or either banner from anywhere, including yourself or shared bank. Relics held by players or in Reliquary cannot be recovered. Pay relic's site cost (3 favor to indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret or burn 2 secrets), then hold it faceup in personal bank. You may hold unlimited relics/banners and peek before choosing.

- **People's Favor:** pay any amount of favor strictly greater than its current favor. Put paid favor on banner; distribute old favor singly to suit banks, starting at any chosen bank, then moving away from the world deck through successive banks and wrapping as needed (the printed bank order). Do not return the old favor to the previous holder. Flip it to normal side if Mob. No seizure penalty when recovering.
- **Darkest Secret:** pay any amount of secrets strictly greater than current secrets. Put paid secrets on it; new holder takes 1 old secret, previous holder takes rest. Recovering from self returns all old secrets to yourself; from shared bank, remainder stays in bank.

Skulls and sacrifices use the actual surviving force, not a subset selected by the number of dice.

1. **Choose defender:** any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there. If no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. A Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. If Chancellor attacks Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for it.
2. **Declare targets, form pools:** at least one target must be at your pawn's site; if defender rules that site you **must** target it. May target any of defender's sites anywhere on map (1 defense die each). If defender's pawn is at your site, may also target any of their relics (printed defense dice), banners (dice equal resources on banner), or pawn-and-favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender's relic target satisfies the local-target requirement. Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in attacking force. Apply relevant modifiers and mandatory title defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2. The mandatory title bonus is itself a Campaign modifier.
3. **Battle plans:** red boxes are attacker-only, blue defender-only, gradient either. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans once each, then defender chooses eligible ruled plans. Plans at a site require rule, not merely pawn presence; bandits use all ruled plans with no cost. A plan can be paid for even with resources on it, but still only used once per Campaign. If an attack die must be removed from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead.
4. **Roll defense:** shields rolled, doubled for each double-symbol (multipliers stack ×2, ×4, ×8...), **plus** all defending warbands at targeted sites, **plus** defender's board force if their pawn is at attacker site or any targeted site. Doubles multiply shields only, not warbands. Bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site.
5. **Roll attack:** each skull immediately kills 1 own force warband. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, leftover single adds zero. May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice **exactly enough to win**, never excess. Attacker wins only if attack **strictly exceeds** defense; tie or lower means defender wins.
6. **Resolve defeat before taking targets:** on attacker victory, the defender first kills half of the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. On defender victory, the attacker kills half its remaining attacking force, rounded down, leaving the survivors on its board; bandits cannot be killed and go into hiding. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects. With Imperial defenders Chancellor chooses which warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay there.

### Citizenship and exile during play

**Grand Scepter:** cannot use its powers the turn you took it. Its holder, even an Exile, may offer Citizenship to any Exile **including themself**, or exile another Citizen. Reliquary relics cannot be campaigned/recovered, their powers cannot be used, and they do not count toward goals while there.

**Offer:** the Grand Scepter cannot make an offer on the turn its current holder took it. In later turns it may offer any Exile, including itself. Must promise **exactly one Reliquary relic**; may additionally negotiate a binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners and non-Reliquary relics. May let recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Other binding-deal powers cannot trade Reliquary relics.

**Acceptance:** flip to Citizen; replace all own warbands on board/map with purple. If insufficient purple, new Citizen chooses which to remove and which to replace. Discard revealed Vision, flip own Usurper title to Oathkeeper, end Act if own turn, and refresh to full leftmost Supply. Exchange promised pieces; Chancellor gains the newly uncovered **mandatory** Reliquary modifier. **Forced Citizenship** powers apply the same status-conversion steps without a negotiated offer: no required Scepter offer or Reliquary relic gift, and no invented promised exchange. Only an actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier. All Imperials rule purple sites; Citizenship does not itself grant a separate shared victory.

**Uncovered Reliquary modifiers, mandatory for Chancellor:** Brutal makes the defeated player kill their entire force when Chancellor attacks, even if Chancellor loses. Decadent makes Provinces/Hinterland-to-Cradle Travel cost no Supply, but Travel to Hinterland costs +1. Careless gives 1 additional favor on every Trade, even when trading for secrets, but 1 fewer secret when trading for secrets. Greedy draws 2 additional Search cards (still stopping at a world Vision) but prohibits Search costing more than 2 Supply.

**Exile another Citizen:** Scepter holder pays them 5 favor, +1 if recipient is Oathkeeper, +1 if recipient holds People's Favor, −1 if payer is Oathkeeper, −1 if payer holds People's Favor (range 3–7). Recipient flips Exile, replaces **board** purple warbands with own color and refreshes full. Purple map garrisons stay Imperial. This does not end their Act by itself.

**Self-exile:** Citizen who does not hold Scepter may give its holder favor equal to own board warbands **plus all their secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards**. Flip Exile, replace board warbands with own color, refresh full, and **end Act**. Cannot self-exile while holding Scepter. Map garrisons stay purple.

## Scoring / Victory Conditions

### Oathkeeper title and four Oaths

The four Oath names are **Supremacy, People, Protection, Devotion**. One Oath is active in

| Oath | Oathkeeper criterion |
|---|---|
| Supremacy | Rule the most sites |
| People | Hold People's Favor |
| Protection | Hold the most relics and banners combined |
| Devotion | Hold Darkest Secret |

For Supremacy, the Chancellor counts all sites ruled by Imperial players. When this collective Imperial count earns the title, the **Chancellor** is its physical holder. Apply the ordinary title-transfer and incumbent-tie rules below.

The four true Vision names are **Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith**. Their correspondence is:

- **Vision of Conquest** matches **Oath of Supremacy**: rule the most sites.
- **Vision of Rebellion** matches **Oath of the People**: hold People's Favor.
- **Vision of Sanctuary** matches **Oath of Protection**: hold the most relics and banners combined.
- **Vision of Faith** matches **Oath of Devotion**: hold Darkest Secret.

### Citizen succession is a separate test

A Citizen wins only by replacing a Chancellor victory with a Successor win. Use the current Oath to select this separate criterion:

| Current Oath | Citizen's Successor goal |
|---|---|
| Supremacy | Hold more relics and banners combined than the Chancellor **and every other Citizen** |
| People | Hold Darkest Secret |
| Protection | Hold People's Favor |
| Devotion | Hold Grand Scepter |

A Citizen does not use the Oathkeeper criterion or a Vision goal as their Successor goal. Meeting the Successor criterion alone never ends the game; it matters when the Chancellor would win.

### Title transfer and victory timing

Current holder keeps title on a tie for its goal. If holder no longer meets goal and several others tie for it, outgoing holder chooses recipient. A new holder always takes it Oathkeeper-side, never Usurper-side. Under Supremacy Chancellor holds it if Empire collectively meets goal; Citizens do not count purple sites separately against each other. Other Oaths concern personal holdings. The Grand Scepter counts as a relic when held; Reliquary relics do not.

**Usurper victory has two timing windows:** at the start of an Exile's turn during Wake, or at the end of round 8 under the endgame priority. From taking Oathkeeper during Act, the normal sequence is next Wake check (not yet Usurper), then flip to Usurper, then win at the following Wake **or at the end of round 8 if that arrives first while still Usurper**. Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence. A title still on Oathkeeper at game end is insufficient.

**Visionary victory:** Exile must have true Vision revealed and goal completed at Wake, with **at least 3 Visions drawn from world deck by all players combined**. This is a shared global count, not a requirement for that Exile to draw three personally. Can reveal it earlier but cannot win early. For Conquest/Sanctuary “most” means **strictly more than every other player**, no ties. Compare to Empire's shared rule for sites. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

**Stable regime:** at ends of rounds 5, 6 and 7, roll end die only if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper. Ends on respectively **6 / 5–6 / 3–6**. Chancellor wins, except a Citizen meeting Successor goal wins **alone instead**. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll.

**War exhaustion:** round 8 ends automatically. Check in this exact priority:

1. If Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper: Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor).
2. Otherwise, Exile Usurper wins.
3. Otherwise, qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins. If several qualify, priority **Conquest → Rebellion → Sanctuary → Faith**.
4. Otherwise Empire wins (Chancellor unless qualified Successor), even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.

Holding Successor goal never ends game on its own. Resolve it whenever Chancellor would win. After victory, write Chronicle below.

### Site powers (Site Reference)

Put 1 secret on it to gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from its suit bank; or put 2 favor to gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser. With no matching adviser, second trade gains zero secrets but still pays 2 favor. Facedown advisers don't match; source limits restrict gains.","### Muster — 1 Supply","### Trade — 1 Supply"],
Q012:["Recover costs 1 Supply plus target cost. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost, then hold it faceup in personal bank. Either banner can be recovered from anywhere, including self/shared bank, by strictly outbidding its current resource count: pay any amount greater than its favor/secrets. For People's Favor, put payment on banner, distribute old favor singly to suit banks starting at a chosen bank and moving away from world deck around order; do not return old favor to prior holder; flip Mob to normal. For Darkest Secret, new holder takes one old secret and previous holder takes remainder; self-recovery returns all old secrets to self; shared-bank remainder stays there. Recovery has no seizure penalty.","### Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost"],
Q013:["To recover another player's Darkest Secret, they must have at least one suited card at their pawn site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers; one unmatched card is sufficient even if others match. An empty site or ruin-only site protects it; ruins/facedown advisers have no suit. If they have no faceup advisers but a suited card is present, it is recoverable. Self/shared-bank recovery ignores this protection.","### Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost"],
Q014:["Defender may be any other player who rules your pawn site or has pawn there; if no player rules it, you may choose bandits. Must target at least one thing at your pawn site; if defender rules that site, must target it. May also target any of defender's sites anywhere (1 defense die each). If defender pawn is at your site, may additionally target their relics, banners, or pawn+favor (2 dice); a relic at that site can itself satisfy local-target requirement. Apply entry/target restrictions such as Narrow Pass/Hidden Place.","### Campaign — 2 Supply","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q015:["Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as their full attacking force warbands; defender pool includes target dice and mandatory title bonus (Oathkeeper +1, Usurper +2), then battle-plan modifiers. Defense is shields (each double-symbol doubles shields, multipliers stack) plus defending warbands at target sites, plus defender board warbands only if defender pawn is at attacker or targeted site; doubles do not multiply warbands. Each attack skull kills one own force warband immediately. Count full swords plus one per pair of hollow swords (odd leftover is zero). May sacrifice own surviving force warbands for +1 each, but exactly enough to win if sacrificing; attack must strictly exceed defense; tie/lower defender wins.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q016:["After attacker wins, first resolve defender defeat: kill half its defending force rounded down, return survivors to board; resolve defeated-plan effects. Then attacker may put any number, including zero, surviving force warbands on targeted sites; zero leaves them to bandits absent another power. Take all targeted relics/banners. For banner seized other than Recover, burn 2 resources down to minimum 1 and flip People's Favor to Mob. If pawn+favor targeted, banishment to legal chosen site is optional and costs no Supply; burning half board favor rounded down is independently optional. Then attacker victory effects; finally discard any plan marked 'At end, discard.'","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q017:["When an Imperial player defends, Chancellor automatically joins; other nonattacking Citizens may join with defender's permission if pawn at attacker or target site. Relevant Campaign modifiers/powers are shared for the defending side; allied board warbands count only when their pawn is at attacker or target site. Allies use their own advisers and Imperial-site plans; each shared plan only once total, one user pays. Declared defender decides order/priority. Chancellor chooses Imperial casualties; surviving site garrisons return to Chancellor board, Citizen board survivors stay there. Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign; Chancellor attacking Citizen makes that Citizen non-Imperial.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q018:["Base Travel costs by origin→destination regions: from Cradle: Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; Provinces: 2/2/2; Hinterland: 4/2/3. Travel to a different site, reveal destination, add its printed favor/secrets from shared bank and printed number of facedown relics from relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then increases/decreases; a power saying spend no Supply is final override, making cost zero. Destination/site entry restrictions remain unless ignored.","### Travel — 1–4 Supply before modifiers"],
Q019:["After the turn Scepter holder took it, Grand Scepter holder may offer any Exile Citizenship, including themself, promising exactly one Reliquary relic; may additionally negotiate binding exchange of favor, secrets, banners, non-Reliquary relics and may allow peeking. Recipient accepts by flipping Citizen, converting own board/map warbands to purple (choosing removals if purple insufficient), discarding revealed Vision, flipping Usurper to Oathkeeper, refreshing full, and ending Act if it is their turn; exchange promised pieces and Chancellor gains newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers use status-conversion steps but need no offer/relic gift or invented exchange.","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q020:["Chronicle Oath: victory by Vision alone means next Oath matches that Vision; otherwise (including multiple victory methods) choose any Oath except current. Exile winner flips all Citizen boards, even boxed, to Exile and may freely offer Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; each accepting player flips board Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. Rebuild top deck as 10 denizens+2 random Visions=12, middle 15+remaining 3 Visions=18, rest denizens below; aid's '12 denizens+2' is incorrect, hence not 14.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q021:["With five players, each suit bank gets 4 favor (3 only for 2–4 players). People's Favor begins normal with 1 favor; Darkest Secret begins with 1 secret; banners in shared bank initially. Chancellor: 2 favor, 1 secret, 3 purple warbands on board and full leftmost Supply. Exile: 1 favor, 1 secret, 3 own-color board warbands and full Supply. Citizen: 1 favor, 1 secret, 3 purple board warbands and full Supply. Later-game Citizens receive no Reliquary relic.","### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)"],
Q022:["Deal saved sites with attached cards Cradle first, then Provinces, Hinterland, each top-down. Chancellor places 2 purple garrisons on top faceup Cradle site and 1 at each other faceup site with a denizen or intact edifice. Resolve printed favor/secret setup prompts at sites from shared bank; if favor insufficient Chancellor allocates it. Existing site relics stay there.","### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)"],
Q023:["Non-Chancellors choose an Exile or Citizen board on its saved side in turn order; Citizen choice is allowed. Each starting pawn location is chosen after drawing setup cards: any faceup site, while Chancellor must choose top Cradle site. Starting Citizens receive no Reliquary relic. Chancellor starts Oathkeeper; for Devotion/People additionally takes Darkest Secret/People's Favor respectively; other banner starts in shared bank.","### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)"],
Q024:["Later game: after deck construction, seed regional discards by taking 3 cards from bottom, one per region pile; each player in turn draws 3 from bottom, chooses one facedown adviser and discards other 2 to normal regional destinations. Advance Visions Drawn for any Vision drawn. Reliquary gets 4 relics drawn and placed randomly, one facedown on each space; not player-chosen.","### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)"],
Q025:["First setup: Plains, Mountain, Rocky Coast faceup (Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland); Lush Coast, Wastes, Salt Flats and other packet sites facedown in marked positions. Pawns: purple on Plains, Red/Blue on Mountain, Yellow on Rocky Coast; 2 purple warbands Plains, 1 each Mountain/Rocky Coast. Longbows, Taming Charm, Elders at those faceup sites. Advisers facedown: Chancellor Forest Paths; Red Animal Playmates; Blue Naysayers; Yellow A Small Favor. Ivory Eye facedown at Mountain.","### First game: preserve the packet order"],
Q026:["Muster and Trade must use an eligible empty card at pawn's site; remote ruled site is insufficient. Normal site Action power access depends on its printed condition, generally rule it or pawn there; powers on advisers you rule are available. Persistent powers with thick braid affect their specified players regardless of ordinary access. Battle plan at a site requires ruling it, not pawn presence alone; you cannot use a plan at your pawn site if you don't rule it.","### Muster — 1 Supply","### Trade — 1 Supply","### Powers, costs and information","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q027:["Outside your turn, paid favor goes immediately to matching bank and secret is placed facedown on your own board (exhausted). It cannot pay another cost until readied faceup during Rest. Battle plan may already have resources and still be paid/used; it remains once per Campaign. Payment exception does not generally permit placing costs on occupied cards for other powers.","### Powers, costs and information","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q028:["Choose ordinary major-action modifiers at action start; use each once for that action in any order. A no-cost modifier may be used on distinct later actions but not twice on one action. Cannot discard an active modifier during that action. Battle plans are a separate Campaign step and each can be used once per Campaign.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q029:["When Played is mandatory after normal site-play favor, then after Homeland reward/modifiers per specific sequence. Ordinary Wake powers resolve once each during Wake, as much as possible; explicit may parts optional. Rest powers are optional once each at end of Rest. A paid power may be used even if its effect does nothing; resolve as much as possible.","### Powers, costs and information","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q030:["Tree restriction means site-only; person means adviser-only, governing faceup play and move/swap. Locked faceup cards cannot be discarded/moved/swapped except Chronicle. Adviser-limit reducers: check against new limit before play; with multiple use the lowest limit, not sum, and respect locked cards. Facedown cards have no restriction banners until faceup.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q031:["Anyone may play Conspiracy faceup; it doesn't replace true Vision. Burn 1 secret to take a relic/banner from a player whose pawn is at your site, only if at least 2 of your faceup advisers match the suit of any of theirs; both may match the same one enemy adviser. Apply banner seizure penalty. Then return Conspiracy to box even if no theft.","### Search — 2–4 Supply"],
Q032:["Cannot freely discard a faceup adviser; only when another rule permits/requires. Drop board warbands only at your pawn site if you rule it; can't drop at empty/bandit site merely by movement. Move any number from own site to board except last physical warband. Citizen pickup requires Chancellor's permission. Imperial players whose pawns are together may give/take board warbands with recipient/other player's permission; same-site Imperial garrisons are all purple, so red and purple site garrisons do not coexist.","### Search — 2–4 Supply","### Minor actions — no Supply","## Components"],
Q033:["May peek at facedown relics at your site without Supply. Once you have peeked at a particular relic, you may peek it again from any site. Grand Scepter holder may peek in Reliquary using its power, except cannot use either Scepter power in the turn they took it.","### Minor actions — no Supply"],
Q034:["Scepter holder pays Citizen 5 favor, +1 if recipient Oathkeeper, +1 if they hold People's Favor, −1 if payer Oathkeeper, −1 if payer holds People's Favor (range 3–7). Citizen flips Exile, replaces only board purple warbands with own-color warbands and refreshes full; purple map garrisons stay. This does not end recipient's Act by itself.","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q035:["Citizen without Scepter may self-exile by giving Scepter holder favor equal to own board warbands plus all own secrets on board and denizen/relic/edifice cards. Flip Exile, replace board warbands with own color, refresh full, end Act. Cannot self-exile while holding Scepter. Map garrisons remain purple.","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q036:["Incumbent keeps title on a tie. If holder later no longer meets criterion and multiple others tie, outgoing holder chooses recipient. In Supremacy, Chancellor holds title when Empire collectively meets goal. Transfer is at end of Campaign, not when temporary site rule changes during resolution.","### Title transfer and victory timing","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q037:["If a plan removes an attack die from an empty attack pool, add a defense die instead. Bandits use all battle plans they rule without cost. Attacker chooses eligible ruled plans first, then defender; Imperial defense follows shared-side rules and declared defender controls order/priority.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q038:["Skulls kill one attacking force warband each immediately. If five were the starting force and S skulls leave R=5−S, subsequent attacker defeat kills floor(R/2), survivors R−floor(R/2) stay on attacker's board; only skull casualties and these defeat casualties leave to their color's personal bank. Defender doesn't take attacker's relics by winning; targets are taken only on attacker victory.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q039:["Defender board warbands contribute only if defender pawn is at attacker site or at any targeted site. Warbands at untargeted sites do not contribute. Shield symbols double shields only (multipliers stack), not warbands added to defense.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q040:["Favor, warbands, cards are limited by available pieces; take/gain only as much as source allows. Secrets and dice are unlimited (use multiplier/reroll as needed). You cannot intentionally burn/give/sacrifice more than prompted amount/cost.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q041:["Facedown card fronts, discard fronts, world-deck count, and world-deck backs below top are private; discard counts/backs, board-resource and warband counts and all else public. Holder may inspect facedown advisers and show them; identity may be discussed or lied about.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q042:["Read literally; Law overrides Playbook/aids except Site Reference; nonitalic rules override italic reminders. Must overrides ordinary rules, cannot overrides even must, ignore overrides named must/cannot; must-if-able has no penalty if unable. Give and Take are separate keywords: restricting one does not restrict other.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q043:["Promises normally are nonbinding and pieces cannot be transferred without rule permission. Exceptions include binding Citizenship offers/deals, expressly binding powers, and Tribunal's negotiated binding immediate favor/secrets exchanges and future actions with agreed penalties; disputed Tribunal breach is settled by coin flip. Tribunal does not permit unrestricted relic/banner transfers or Reliquary relics outside the stated rules. Exchange alone is optional permission, not a forced/equal trade.","### Powers, costs and information","### Site powers (Site Reference)","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q044:["Brutal: when Chancellor attacks, defeated player kills entire force even if Chancellor loses. Decadent: Provinces/Hinterland→Cradle costs no Supply, but Travel to Hinterland +1. Careless: +1 favor on every Trade (including secrets trade), but −1 secret when trading for secrets. Greedy: Search draws 2 extra (still stops at world Vision), but prohibits Search costing >2 Supply.","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q045:["Imperial winner may build or repair one edifice. Build at a ruled site with no intact or ruined edifice, replacing its denizen with matching intact Archive edifice and returning denizen to world deck; or flip a ruled ruin intact. A site already containing ruin cannot get a new edifice by replacement; it can only repair that ruin.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q046:["Discard all sites except those winner rules or with an intact edifice; shuffle discarded sites into site deck, discard attached denizens, return attached relics to relic deck, ruined edifices to Archive. At retained sites winner doesn't rule, flip intact edifice to ruin and discard all denizens there. Set aside all ruin sites with attached ruin, remaining denizens and relics for repacking.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q047:["After excluding set-aside ruins, fill Cradle top-down by pushing Cradle sites up then importing Provinces then Hinterland top-down. Fill Provinces top-down by pushing up then importing Hinterland top-down; push Hinterland sites up. Fill empty Hinterland bottom-up with set-aside ruins bottom-up, then empty Provinces slots similarly. Remaining slots get facedown site-deck cards; in each region with no faceup site, flip top site faceup.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q048:["Winner's most common adviser suit: 3 random cards from matching Archive; next clockwise suit 2, next clockwise 1, totaling six. Winner chooses among tied most-common suits; no suited advisers means choose any suit. Suit order Discord→Arcane→Order→Hearth→Beast→Nomad→Discord.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q049:["No partial allocation: if Archive cannot supply the full allocation for a suit, add none of that allocation and heal Archive instead. Sort Dispossessed by suit; take 6 random from the largest Dispossessed suit stack into world deck; shuffle remaining Dispossessed into matching Archive stacks.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q050:["Set aside all five Visions including Conspiracy. Shuffle all discard piles together with losing players' advisers, remove 6 random unseen cards to Dispossessed. Winner's advisers are excluded. Then continue with relic cleanup/world deck steps.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q051:["Save Grand Scepter in World Box; return losing players' relics to relic deck and shuffle. Refill faceup sites with fewer relics than printed R icons up to number, facedown. Shuffle winner's remaining relics with Reliquary relics and stack atop relic deck.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q052:["Stack each site's attached cards on it; stack sites top Cradle through bottom Hinterland and save in World Box. Save boards on current Exile/Citizen sides. Next game can have different people; after seating, non-Chancellors choose among saved boards on saved sides in turn order, no automatic former-owner inheritance.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q053:["Yes, different-suit discard does not suppress Homeland reward; suppression requires discarding a card of the same suit at that site this turn. Matching-suit play gives printed Homeland reward (shared-bank secret, suit-bank favor, 2 warbands, or relic treated as Recover). Sequence: normal site-play favor, Homeland reward, then card's When Played. Relic reward costs neither Supply nor usual site resource cost.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q054:["Traveling from one Coast to another costs 1 Supply and ignores Narrow Pass. Destination alone being Coast is not enough; origin and destination must both be Coasts.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q055:["Must travel to Narrow Pass when entering its region from another region; when targeting anything in its region from another region, must also target Narrow Pass unless you rule it. Ruling it only removes the Campaign-target requirement, not entry travel requirement.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q056:["To travel to Hidden Place or declare a Campaign target there, flip 1 secret on your board facedown; the exhausted secret stays there until Rest. Buried Giant travel power can ignore Narrow Pass, Shrouded Wood ignores Narrow Pass/Hidden Place for its fixed-origin travel, and a named power saying ignore can override; ordinary travel modifiers do not inherently waive Hidden Place. (Buried Giant's permission itself only states Narrow Pass.)","### Site powers (Site Reference)","### Travel — 1–4 Supply before modifiers"],
Q057:["From Buried Giant, may flip 1 own board secret facedown to pay no Supply and ignore Narrow Pass. Secret remains exhausted on board until Rest. This permission names Narrow Pass only; it does not automatically waive Hidden Place.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q058:["Search while your pawn is at Marshes draws 1 fewer card. Merely ruling Marshes remotely does not trigger this pawn-location condition.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q059:["At Great Slum, when playing or moving a card there, may first discard a card there. This does not grant general discard permission at unrelated times.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q060:["Shrouded Wood has fixed base travel cost 2 before other modifiers, ignoring Narrow Pass/Hidden Place. If enemy rules it, ruler chooses where traveler goes (Chancellor chooses for Empire), including forced travel/banishment. Banishment spends no Supply but destination-choice rule still applies.","### Site powers (Site Reference)","### Travel — 1–4 Supply before modifiers","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q061:["Plains/Mountain require add/subtract one attack die when the site or anything at site is targeted, even if attacker rules it; not limited to targeting site itself.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q062:["Muster at River gives one additional warband if you rule it. Without rule, ordinary Muster gives 2 but not the extra one.","### Site powers (Site Reference)","### Muster — 1 Supply"],
Q063:["From Provinces to Hinterland base 2, plus Charming Valley's +1 from traveling from it, total 3 Supply before other modifiers. If any applicable power says spend no Supply, final Travel Supply is zero despite increases.","### Site powers (Site Reference)","### Travel — 1–4 Supply before modifiers"],
Q064:["Tribunal Action is available if you rule it or your pawn is there. It permits binding immediate exchanges of favor/secrets, and binding future actions with any player with agreed penalties; disputed breach settled by coin flip. It doesn't grant unrestricted relic/banner transfers.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q065:["Bandit Crown treats bandits as own warbands: rule empty faceup sites, may pick up last physical site warband, add relevant bandits to defense (or attack force with suitable power). Bandits cannot be killed, moved, sacrificed, including for skulls or battle-plan costs.","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q066:["Facedown sites cannot be ruled or hold cards, so move powers cannot place cards there. Both intact and ruined edifices count toward site's capacity; ruin has no suit and cannot be used for Muster or Trade.","## Components","### Muster — 1 Supply","### Trade — 1 Supply"],
Q067:["No. Corrected Draw keyword is simply draw from top of prompted source, not entire Search procedure. Whenever Vision drawn from world deck, always advance Visions Drawn (including Oracle); Search action itself still stops at its first world-deck Vision.","### Powers, costs and information","### Search — 2–4 Supply"],
Q068:["Act may include any number of major actions, minor actions, and Action powers, in any order/repeating/none if costs paid; finish an action before beginning another. Supply may remain unspent; after refresh, add unspent Supply capped at leftmost.","### Act"],
Q069:["Seizing banner by non-Recover method triggers seizure penalty: burn 2 resources to minimum 1; People's Favor flips Mob. Recover has no seizure penalty and instead requires paying strictly more than current banner resource amount; old banner resources are redistributed/allocated per banner rules.","### Campaign — 2 Supply","### Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost"],
Q070:["Yes, a restrictive plan may need to be declared first, but in Imperial defense the declared defender chooses order, timing and priority when Allies disagree, including whether restrictive plan must go first and who uses shared plan. A plan can only be activated once total per Campaign by one user who pays.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q071:["On Citizenship conversion, new Citizen chooses which own warbands to remove and which to replace if insufficient purple. If later exiled, replace board purple warbands with their own color; purple site garrisons remain unchanged.","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q072:["Given normal-side banner at five, adding one is the single Wake choice; at six it flips to Mob only after choices, with no retroactive second choice. If already Mob, repeat the choice twice: two choices before threshold check.","### Wake: mandatory order","### Recover — 1 Supply plus target cost"],
Q073:["Unrevealed Vision doesn't qualify; it must be revealed. Revealing true Vision is an Act minor action, not Wake, so cannot reveal at Wake to claim immediate Wake victory. If fewer than 3 world-deck Visions have been drawn globally, no Visionary win even with revealed Vision and goal met.","### Search — 2–4 Supply","### Title transfer and victory timing"],
Q074:["Scenario: at round-eight check title is still Oathkeeper-side for Exile; it does not win as Usurper. Apply priority: Empire wins if Chancellor/Citizen Oathkeeper (Citizen Successor can replace); otherwise Usurper only if already Usurper; then Vision; else Empire fallback (Citizen Successor can replace).","### Title transfer and victory timing",{"given_state":"Exile's title has not flipped to Usurper at round-eight check.","completed_events":"Round eight has ended; evaluate final priority.","next_operation":"Check round-eight priority.","calculation":"None.","result":"Exile does not win as Usurper; resolve Empire/qualified Citizen Successor first, then qualifying revealed Vision, otherwise Empire fallback."}],
Q075:["No. Multiple victory methods means choose any next Oath except current, even if Vision was one method. Exile Chronicle winner may offer free Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped from Citizen; cannot offer self. Acceptors flip Citizen and replace each garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q076:["No: People’s Favor permits discard from any site in your region, then play at any site in your region, so they may differ. Discard may be from a different region than pawn (but destination uses card's region cycle). Locked card cannot be discarded absent exception; respect locks.","### Search — 2–4 Supply","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q077:["All listed effects are optional after attacker wins: may banish if pawn+favor targeted, may independently burn half board favor rounded down, and may take all targeted banners (targets must be taken). If burning, remove floor(board favor/2); banishment and burn are separate decisions.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q078:["Skulls kill own warbands from entire attacking force regardless of number of attack dice rolled; fewer dice doesn't select smaller force. Sacrifice can add attack, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra; cannot use excess sacrifices to reduce upkeep.","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q079:["Refresh depends on warbands remaining in personal bank, not board/map count. Chancellor: 18+ gives 6; 11–17 gives 5; 4–10 gives 4; 0–3 gives 3. Exile: 9+ gives 6; 4–8 gives 5; 0–3 gives 4. Then save unspent Supply one marker space left per point, capped at leftmost.","### Rest: mandatory order"],
Q080:["Attacker-only red, defender-only blue, either-role gradient boxes. Ruling a plan alone doesn't permit wrong-role use; must be eligible for role and rule it (bandits use ruled plans without cost).","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q081:["For Chancellor/Citizens, enemies are Exiles, not fellow Imperials. Citizen attacking Chancellor/another Citizen and Chancellor attacking a Citizen makes specified participant non-Imperial for that Campaign. Intra-Empire doesn't make all Citizens non-Imperial. In Campaign, 'your enemy' means opposing side, including defender and Allies against attacker.","### Site powers (Site Reference)","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q082:["Scenario: source has 3 available cards and no stop/reduction. You cannot voluntarily stop at 1; draw 3. If source runs out, draw only remaining cards. Search also draws fewer only for Vision stop or draw reduction.","### Search — 2–4 Supply",{"given_state":"Three cards available; no Vision encountered and no draw-reducing modifier.","completed_events":"Search has begun.","next_operation":"Continue drawing until three cards drawn.","calculation":"3 requested, 3 available = 3 drawn.","result":"Must draw all three; if source exhausted earlier, take only what remains."}],
Q083:["Round marker starts round 1 and Visions Drawn at zero. Chancellor starts each round; turns proceed clockwise, each turn Wake→Act→Rest. After all players acted, check round-end victory, then if play continues advance round marker; round eight ends automatically.","### First game: preserve the packet order","### Later games: use the Chronicled world (Law §1)","### Turn Structure"],
Q084:["No later-game bottom-deck seed/adviser procedure in first-game packet setup. Keep prepared packet/decks ordered, don't shuffle; place 3/3/5 ordered packet cards in Cradle/Provinces/Hinterland discards; remaining 41 denizen/Vision cards from packet B stay ordered in world deck. Ivory Eye Mountain facedown; next 4 relics facedown on Reliquary, remaining 15 relic deck.","### First game: preserve the packet order"],
Q085:["Before first Chronicle, open Archive packet: place 8 cardboard dividers in small-box compartment; put edifices in matching sections; separately shuffle each suit's denizens into its Archive section.","### Writing the Chronicle (Law §8, with base errata)"],
Q086:["Forced Citizenship doesn't require Grand Scepter offer, Reliquary gift, or promised exchange. It still applies status conversion: flip Citizen; replace own board/map warbands purple (remove as needed), discard revealed Vision, flip Usurper to Oathkeeper, refresh full Supply, and end Act if own turn; Chancellor gains newly uncovered mandatory modifier only when a Reliquary relic is actually removed.","### Citizenship and exile during play"],
Q087:["Ordinarily cannot put favor/secrets on a card already holding either resource, including to pay a normal Action/modifier power; battle-plan payment is exception. A no-cost power may still be used despite resources already on card. Outside-turn payment goes favor to matching bank and secrets facedown on your board.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q088:["Title holder mandatory defense bonus: Oathkeeper +1 defense die, Usurper +2; applies as Campaign modifier. Under Supremacy Chancellor is physical title holder when Empire collectively qualifies; Imperial defenders also share Oathkeeper defense bonus even if an ally's title, through shared Imperial defense powers.","### Campaign — 2 Supply","### Oathkeeper title and four Oaths"],
Q089:["Move/swap must obey capacity, placement, tree/person restrictions and locks. Move/swap alone is not play: no site-play favor and no When Played power; explicit play instruction does trigger normal play effects.","### Powers, costs and information"],
Q090:["When Citizen purple warband is killed (skull, sacrifice, defeat), send it to that color's personal bank—purple goes to Chancellor. Surviving defeated force follows Imperial-defense rule: surviving site warbands return to Chancellor's board; surviving warbands already on Citizen board stay there.","### Powers, costs and information","### Campaign — 2 Supply"],
Q091:["Bandits rule faceup sites without physical warbands but do not compete for victory. Most-site comparisons are among players; bandits cannot hold Oathkeeper/Vision goal and don't prevent a player qualifying among players.","## Components","### Oathkeeper title and four Oaths"],
Q092:["At end of your Wake, if pawn at Salt Flats, Mine, or Drowned City, optionally take one token total: either one favor or one secret from that site, if available. Remote rule provides none; empty site gives nothing and no bank substitute.","### Wake: mandatory order","### Site powers (Site Reference)"],
Q093:["Scenario: attacker lost; after roll first apply defeat casualties, then defeated battle-plan effects. Here defender's 'If you're victorious' resolves after defeat; attacker has no victorious effect.
